newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor buys Brazilian cement businesses.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor buys Brazilian cement businesses.

text.p: Portugal's biggest cement producer Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal said it had acquired two Brazilian cement businesses for 62 billion escudos ($394 million).
It said in a statement that it had acquired CISAFRA, a cement producer, and the SERRANA group's cement business.
The two acquisitions represent total cement assets, including shareholders' equity, financial debt and investments in progress, of $177 per ton of production capacity.
Cimpor said the production capacity of the acquired businesses would reach about three million tons per year.

Cimpor's cement production capacity in Portugal, Spain, Mozambique, Morocco and Brazil would stand at 11 million tonnes per year and total sales would be nine million tons per year after the latest acquisitions.
In the medium term Brazil is expected to represent 14 percent of Cimpor's turnover and 16 percent of its operating income, the company said.
Cimpor said it had purchased, directly and indirectly, shares representing 67.3 percent of CISAFRA's capital and 99.97 percent of its voting rights.

A new company will be created for SERRANA's cement business, it said. Cimpor has signed a contract under which it guarantees the acquisition of shares representing 76.6 percent of the new company's capital.
According to the deal made with Bunge Group, the Cimpor assumes an obligation to launch a bid for the remaining shares as soon as legal requirements are fulfilled.
CISAFRA owns a cement plant in the Brazil's Bahia state and distribution terminals in several regions where it operates.
SERRANA's cement business includes two cement plants, one in the state of Sao Paulo and the other in the state of Rio Grande do Sul where it also owns a milling facility.
Cimpor said that after the acquisitions it would be operating in the northeast, southeast and south of Brazil with a market share of five percent.
"With this investment, Cimpor pursues its internationalisation strategy, as previously presented to its shareholders," the company said.
"The company is diversifying the geographic area of its operations through acquisitions outside Portugal and Galicia in high growth markets with different economic cycles," it added.
